observed_vs_expected: Expected observations forecast a monotonic increase in best_target_score as the reference wavelength approaches 550 nm, with stable valid_candidates and a positive tightest_margin. Actual execution produced highly volatile scores [0.8497367027464725, 0.6163349648355376, 0.9093890026693847, 0.6859039582588472], culminating in a -0.2234850444105375 regression from round 3 to round 4. Valid candidates remained stable at 9, and tightest_margin stayed strongly positive at 0.48351970274442685, confirming structural feasibility despite the spectral performance drop.
deviation_mechanism: The optimization algorithm applied overly aggressive step sizes, causing uncoordinated thickness displacements that destroyed quarter-wave phase accumulation across both target bands. When spacer layers shift rapidly outside their designed optical half-wavelengths, the accumulated phase error converts constructive interference into destructive overlap, collapsing the broadband coupling efficiency regardless of individual layer adjustments. This step-driven interference breakdown explains the score volatility rather than any fundamental material or topological limit.
continue_rationale: Four rounds have been executed with 9 valid candidates persisting and a healthy tightest_margin of 0.48351970274442685 nm. The recent score regression does not indicate physical infeasibility or constraint saturation; instead, it reveals an unstable search trajectory driven by excessive optimizer step magnitudes. Continuing with constrained stepping allows the system to recover the phase-matched states observed in round 3 without risking premature termination of a viable topology.
insight_for_next: Reduce maximum per-layer perturbation range by 50% and implement a cooldown schedule that locks outer-most layers after 2 iterations. Reinitialize the population using adaptive quarter-wave seed thicknesses calculated from the weighted average refractive indices observed in round 3, ensuring initial guesses respect the local dispersion properties before optimization proceeds.
insight_grounding: Audit trail from candidate_thicknesses_nm confirms step-size-driven breakdown: the candidate recorded in round 3 (candidate_thicknesses_nm index 2), layer 15 had a thickness of 88.27197548558794 nm, which expanded to 102.50399578799696 nm in round 4 (candidate_thicknesses_nm index 3), layer 15 (+14.23 nm). These >16 nm swings directly correlate with the best_target_score dropping from 0.9093890026693847 to 0.6859039582588472.
